name: Kit Curtis
life: “I still remember calculating a week's wages in taxi receipts.” Friday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Kit stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I have been paying taxi fares with credit. I showed the crew my actual monthly statement before the vote.
appearance: Kit has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a moss-green cardigan with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring. In conversation Kit counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Kit loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To get through winter without further credit fares.
family: Gale Levin is Kit’s stepsibling. Kit brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Gale makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *One sleeve short*, Gale says, “I paid for a matching cuff lining on condition the customer never learns my name.”
connections: Sylvia Kang. The worker living on costly taxis takes an actual statement to the person checking the clock rounding.
